findings: Both captures describe Stripe's MoR service for digital products, with indirect tax, fraud, disputes and transaction-level customer support handled by Stripe under the product’s scope. Other Stripe products keep the business as MoR, with Tax, Radar, Payments/disputes and Connect as comparison routes. Checkout and Payment Links are the Managed Payments comparison-table checkout surfaces, Billing is listed for subscriptions on both sides, and new Checkout, updating Checkout, Payment Links and mobile app are use cases in both (old raw lines 6–36, new raw lines 7–42). Link is the separately described customer-facing Sold through Link identity, with merchants retaining product-level support (related How It Works lines 11–23).

The only newly explicit support/status statement beyond the old prose and restrictions is the comparison's Other Stripe products transaction-level support cell, blank in April overview and explicitly Unsupported in November. Managed fraud/disputes checks and platform Unsupported make previously stated responsibility/exclusions explicit rather than showing launch or removal (old raw lines 25–43, new raw lines 31–49). The mapped source already recorded some formerly blank entries as negative, but leaves Managed fraud/disputes cells blank despite its prose (source lines 17–35).

The separate tax guide lines 26–28 assigns indirect tax on all domestic sales to Japan-based sellers. For Singapore-based sellers, the exception covers domestic B2B sales when the customer identifies the purchase as business at checkout. Route these predicates reciprocally through `wiki/concepts/stripe-managed-payments.md`: lines 50–52 already distinguish them, and the tax-guide route at line 117 compresses both into “Japan/Singapore B2B exceptions”. Keep the overview’s more-than-80-country indirect-tax coverage separately scoped from the April 22, 2026 merchant GA announcement for businesses in 39 countries (November changelog lines 32–36), and from account, product and transaction eligibility. The separate eligibility guide requires direct account integration and eligibility review, eligible geography, directly sold fully automated digital products, legal rights and eligible tax codes (lines 7–20, 70–102). The tax guide also assigns the seller responsibility where Stripe cannot assume indirect-tax liability and identifies Stripe Tax as the compatible solution there (lines 7–30, 134–159).

Both captures exclude Connect, Elements-style embeddable/advanced components, specified Customer-object invoice operations, creating subscriptions outside Checkout or Payment Links and third-party tax systems (old raw lines 38–47, new raw lines 44–55). Embedded Checkout remains a distinct supported UI in the separate November migration guide (lines 9–18). The mobile use case is routed to a qualified iOS-to-browser hosted Checkout integration for some countries in a separate guide (mobile lines 5–34), not a claim of native Elements or every market/platform. Subscription migration is new purchases only in that guide. Neither Session creation, redirect, app-to-web sample nor Billing support cell proves payment or entitlement.

Reciprocal scope is wiki/index.md line 7 → wiki/stripe-index.md lines 130–138 and 788 → wiki/concepts/stripe-managed-payments.md lines 60–91 and 113–123. The current source's line 49 drops the separate Customer-object one-off invoice limitation; keep it explicit as well as billing-period wording, category-qualified subscription invoice/site changelog exceptions and neither generalized prohibition nor expanded permission.

The separately captured November Checkout migration guide lines 9–18 requires API `2025-03-31.basil` or later for updating an existing hosted or embedded Checkout page integration that creates Checkout Sessions server-side in `payment` or `subscription` mode. The guide also scopes subscription eligibility to new purchases through a Managed Payments Checkout Session. This floor applies to that migration path. Keep the embedded Checkout page distinct from excluded Elements, and the mobile pointer scoped to the separate iOS app-to-browser Checkout instructions in supported markets.

The October 5, 2026 Pay Invoice changelog entry (lines 9–13) allows finalizing and attempting payment on a Managed Payments invoice with its already associated payment method. The request cannot provide a different payment method or other payment-related parameters. Treat this as a dated payment-attempt operation, separate from final payment outcome and from overview restrictions on creating invoices or attaching items to Customer objects. Preserve the April 22 item additions on eligible Managed Payments subscription invoices and subscriptions within their separate object and operation scope.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments, the April 23 and November 7, 2026 overviews describe Stripe as merchant of record for eligible digital products, handling sales tax/VAT/GST in more than 80 countries, fraud, disputes and transaction-level support. With other Stripe products the business remains merchant of record, using Tax, Radar, Payments or Connect as appropriate. Checkout and Payment Links are compared as Managed Payments checkout surfaces, Billing is listed for subscriptions, and both pages route new or existing Checkout, Payment Links and mobile app use. Link is the customer-facing identity in the separate How It Works guide. The separate eligibility and tax guides qualify direct accounts, business geography, eligible fully automated digital products and tax codes, and domestic tax exceptions. Japan-based sellers are responsible for indirect tax on all domestic sales. For Singapore-based sellers, the exception covers domestic B2B sales, identified by the customer at checkout (separate tax guide lines 26-28). The 80-plus indirect-tax coverage is distinct from the April 22, 2026 GA milestone for businesses in 39 countries (old raw lines 6-36 and new raw lines 7-42). Both overviews exclude Connect, Elements-style or advanced integrations, Customer-object invoice-item attachments, one-off invoices on a Customer or outside the billing period, subscription creation outside Checkout or Payment Links, and third-party tax solutions. Embedded Checkout page is a distinct supported documented route in the separate migration guide. Eligibility, a Session, a supported row or an invoice payment attempt do not prove a paid transaction (old raw lines 38-47 and new raw lines 44-55). `source-stripe-managed-payments-overview.md` preserves the main comparison and uses but leaves fraud/dispute cells blank and omits the one-off Customer-object condition.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments, November makes the comparison explicit: it fills the fraud/dispute and Managed platform cells consistently with April prose, and changes the other-products transaction-level support cell from blank to Unsupported. These are clarified documentation labels rather than evidence of rollout. Changed headings, links, table styling and the expanded tax names are presentation/navigation (old raw lines 6-36 and new raw lines 7-42). Keep April as dated in `source-stripe-managed-payments-overview.md` and add reciprocal Managed Payments and changelog scope. Both overviews prohibit the Customer-object invoice-item route and one-off invoices on a Customer or outside the billing period. The April 22 changelog separately permits eligible Invoice Items and Invoice Line Items on Managed Payments subscription invoices and eligible Subscription Items on those subscriptions. The separate October 5, 2026 Pay Invoice changelog says the endpoint finalizes and attempts payment using the method already associated with the invoice. The request cannot specify a different payment method or include other payment-related parameters (changelog lines 9-13). A payment attempt is distinct from a final payment outcome and from restricted invoice creation (old raw lines 38-47 and new raw lines 44-55). Keep embedded Checkout separate from Elements and the mobile pointer scoped to the separately described iOS app-to-browser Checkout in supported markets. The separate November migration guide requires API `2025-03-31.basil` or later for existing hosted or embedded Checkout integrations that create Checkout Sessions server-side in `payment` or `subscription` mode (migration guide lines 9-18). Retain the separate Session/payment-state and product/geographic qualifications. Overview links do not establish account access, a deployed SDK or API change, settlement, or blanket tax coverage (old raw lines 12-21 and new raw lines 13-27).
